title: A new face
paragraphs: Everybody has looked in the mirror at some point in their lives and thought they could do with a smaller nose or fewer wrinkles. Almost 10 million operations were performed in 2014, according to the International Society of Aesthetic Plastic Surgery. Eyelid surgery topped the list of the five most popular procedures, which included breast augmentation and rhinoplasty.

We hear a lot about cosmetic surgery these days. But what many people may not realise is that reconstructing someone's face has an ancient past. There are reports of treatments to restore a broken nose in ancient Egyptian documents. Considering that safe anaesthetics and antibiotics were only discovered in the 19th and 20th centuries, it was a truly painful and risky business to go under the knife in the past.

But as far back as the mid-15th century nose jobs were carried out using skin taken from the upper arm. Plastic surgery went through a revolution during World War One. The trenches protected the soldiers' bodies, but many who stuck their heads up were exposed to explosions. New techniques were developed by Harold Gillies who ran a ward at the Cambridge Military Hospital in Britain, and later a whole hospital dedicated to helping disfigured soldiers.

Many wounded men at that time couldn't stand looking at their own faces. There were no mirrors in the hospital. In parks near the hospital, some benches were painted blue to signal to patients with facial injuries that they could sit there. And it was a way of telling local residents to prepare for the shock of seeing someone with a disfigured face.

Plastic surgery has come a long way since then. It reconstructs what does need reconstructing but it also makes people with no particular problems feel more confident. Bigger breasts? Straight nose? Facelift? In many cases, cosmetic surgery isn't a necessity at all, just a choice. But when done properly by capable doctors on patients who have a realistic goal, it's believed that plastic surgery can heal psychological wounds almost as much as physical ones.

vocabulary.example: She used cream to reduce wrinkles around her eyes.
vocabulary.translation: 她用面霜来减少眼角的皱纹。

vocabulary.term: aesthetic [iːsˈθetɪk] adj. 美容的，美学的
vocabulary.entry: aesthetic [iːsˈθetɪk] adj. 美容的，美学的
vocabulary.example: The clinic offers various aesthetic treatments for skin care.
vocabulary.translation: 这家诊所提供多种美容护肤项目。

vocabulary.term: plastic surgery [ˈplæstɪk ˈsɜːdʒəri] n. 整形手术
vocabulary.entry: plastic surgery [ˈplæstɪk ˈsɜːdʒəri] n. 整形手术
vocabulary.example: He underwent plastic surgery to repair his injured nose.
vocabulary.translation: 他接受了整形手术来修复受伤的鼻子。

vocabulary.term: eyelid surgery [ˈaɪlɪd ˈsɜːdʒəri] n. 眼睑手术
vocabulary.entry: eyelid surgery [ˈaɪlɪd ˈsɜːdʒəri] n. 眼睑手术
vocabulary.example: Eyelid surgery is a common procedure to correct sagging skin.
vocabulary.translation: 眼睑手术是矫正皮肤松弛的常见手术。

vocabulary.term: breast augmentation [brest ˌɔːɡmenˈteɪʃn] n. 隆胸手术
vocabulary.entry: breast augmentation [brest ˌɔːɡmenˈteɪʃn] n. 隆胸手术
vocabulary.example: Breast augmentation is one of the most popular cosmetic surgeries.
vocabulary.translation: 隆胸手术是最受欢迎的美容手术之一。

vocabulary.example: She had rhinoplasty to reshape her nose for a natural look.
vocabulary.translation: 她做了鼻整形术，将鼻子重塑成自然的样子。

vocabulary.term: cosmetic surgery [kɒzˈmetɪk ˈsɜːdʒəri] n. 整容手术
vocabulary.entry: cosmetic surgery [kɒzˈmetɪk ˈsɜːdʒəri] n. 整容手术
vocabulary.example: Many people choose cosmetic surgery to improve their appearance.
vocabulary.translation: 很多人选择整容手术来改善外貌。

vocabulary.example: Surgeons worked hard to reconstruct the patient’s damaged face.
vocabulary.translation: 外科医生努力修复患者受损的面部。

vocabulary.example: The doctor administered an anaesthetic before the operation.
vocabulary.translation: 医生在手术前使用了麻醉剂。

vocabulary.example: Antibiotics are used to prevent infection after surgery.
vocabulary.translation: 抗生素用于预防手术后的感染。

vocabulary.term: go under the knife [ɡəʊ ˈʌndə ðə naɪf] phr. 接受手术
vocabulary.entry: go under the knife [ɡəʊ ˈʌndə ðə naɪf] phr. 接受手术
vocabulary.example: She was nervous about going under the knife for the first time.
vocabulary.translation: 她第一次接受手术，感到很紧张。

vocabulary.example: Soldiers hid in the trenches to avoid enemy attacks.
vocabulary.translation: 士兵们躲在战壕里躲避敌人的攻击。

vocabulary.example: The fire left him permanently disfigured on his arms.
vocabulary.translation: 火灾导致他手臂永久毁容。

vocabulary.example: An old man sat on the park bench reading a newspaper.
vocabulary.translation: 一位老人坐在公园长椅上看报纸。

vocabulary.term: facelift [ˈfeɪslɪft] n. 面部拉皮手术
vocabulary.entry: facelift [ˈfeɪslɪft] n. 面部拉皮手术
vocabulary.example: Her facelift made her look much younger than her age.
vocabulary.translation: 面部拉皮手术让她看起来比实际年龄年轻很多。

vocabulary.example: Water and food are basic necessities for human survival.
vocabulary.translation: 水和食物是人类生存的基本必需品。

vocabulary.example: She is a capable doctor with rich surgical experience.
vocabulary.translation: 她是一位有能力的医生，拥有丰富的手术经验。

vocabulary.example: It’s important to set realistic goals for cosmetic surgery.
vocabulary.translation: 为整容手术设定现实的目标很重要。

vocabulary.term: psychological wound [ˌsaɪkəˈlɒdʒɪkl wuːnd] n. 心理创伤
vocabulary.entry: psychological wound [ˌsaɪkəˈlɒdʒɪkl wuːnd] n. 心理创伤
vocabulary.example: Counseling can help heal the psychological wounds of trauma.
vocabulary.translation: 心理辅导有助于治愈创伤带来的心理创伤。

vocabulary.example: The treatment aims to improve both physical and mental health.
vocabulary.translation: 这种治疗旨在改善身心健康。

sentences.chinese: 古埃及文献中就有关于修复鼻梁断裂的治疗方法的记载。

sentences.chinese: 在医院附近的公园里，一些长椅被涂成蓝色，以向面部受伤的患者示意他们可以坐在那里。

sentences.chinese: 这也是告诉当地居民，让看到毁容的人做好心理准备。

sentences.chinese: 从那时起，整形手术已经取得了长足的进步。

sentences.chinese: 它不仅重塑了需要修复的部位，也让那些没有特别问题的人感到更加自信。

sentences.english: Facelift?

sentences.chinese: 在许多情况下，美容手术根本不是必需品，而只是一种选择。

sentences.english: But when done properly by capable doctors on patients who have a realistic goal, it's believed that plastic surgery can heal psychological wounds almost as much as physical ones.
sentences.chinese: 但如果由有能力的医生为有现实目标的患者进行手术，人们相信整形手术可以同样有效地治愈心理创伤和身体创伤。
